text: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that not a single gap was left in it—though at that time I had not yet set the doors in the gates—

Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let us meet together at Hakkephirim^ in the plain of Ono." But they were plotting to do me harm.

^ Or "in one of the villages"; the Hebrew word can be read either as a place name or as a common noun.

versions.text: Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let us meet together at Hakkephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were plotting to do me harm.
versions.explanation: The unexplained transliteration "Hakkephirim" gives a listener no information; a short footnote noting the alternative reading ("one of the villages") helps without changing the text.

text: So I sent messengers to them with this reply: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"
Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave them the same answer.
The fifth time, Sanballat sent his servant to me with the same message, and in his hand was an open letter.

In it was written: "It is reported among the nations—and Geshem says it too—that you and the Jews are planning to revolt, and that this is why you are building the wall. They say you intend to make yourself their king,
and that you have even set up prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will reach the king. So come, let us confer together."
Then I sent him this reply: "Nothing of what you say has happened. You are inventing it all out of your own head."

They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will never be finished." But now, my God,^ strengthen my hands.

^ The words "my God" are not in the Hebrew, which reads simply "But now, strengthen my hands"; they are supplied because the line is a prayer.

versions.text: They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will fall slack, and the work will never be finished." But now, my God, strengthen my hands.
versions.explanation: "My God" is an addition not present in the Hebrew text; a brief footnote makes this explicit. Also, "from the work" (מִן־הַמְּלָאכָה) is part of the quoted taunt and is currently absorbed into the following clause.

text: Then I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in there. He said, "Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us bar the temple doors, for they are coming to kill you—tonight they are coming to kill you."
But I said, "Should a man like me run away? And who like me could enter the temple and live? I will not go!"

versions.text: But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Should a man like me go into the temple to save his life? I will not go!"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew וָחָי ("and live") does not say "to save his life"; the point is that a layman like Nehemiah entering the sanctuary would not survive, not that he would be preserved by entering. The current wording reverses the sense of the clause.

versions.text: But I said, "Should a man like me run away? And who, being such as I, could go into the temple and live? I will not go!"
versions.explanation: The clause "who, being such as I," is stiff and hard to read aloud; the Hebrew מִי כָמוֹנִי is a simple "who like me," which preserves the parallel with "a man like me" in the previous clause and flows better in oral reading.

text: I realized that God had not sent him; he had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He was hired to make me afraid, so that I would do this and sin, and they would have an evil report to spread and could hold me in contempt.
Remember, my God, what Tobiah and Sanballat have done—and Noadiah the prophetess as well, and the rest of the prophets who tried to frighten me.
So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid, and their confidence sank low, for they knew that this work had been accomplished by our God.

versions.text: When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid and fell greatly in their own esteem, for they knew that this work had been accomplished by our God.
versions.explanation: "Fell greatly in their own esteem" is stiff for oral reading; a smoother idiom keeps the sense of the Hebrew "they fell much in their own eyes" while reading aloud naturally.

text: In those days, too, the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah kept coming to them,
for many in Judah were bound to him by oath, since he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They kept praising his good deeds in my presence and reporting my words back to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
